question: Does the preference between the existing whole-session activity and temporal skill reverse between questions supported by the first and second halves of the same source? This diagnoses a reason to collect actual finer-span interventions.
population: All 60 original physical skill contrasts (452 question comparisons) from six training dialogues; keep early four-path contrasts separate from randomized donors and the later 40-window/378-question forward panel. Each whole-session measured return stays intact. No independent data, actor selection or model training.
placement: Split the pivot session at the internal even turn boundary closest to its midpoint; break equal distances by the earlier boundary. This preserves original adjacent-turn pairs. Label a question first or second when all its evidence in the pivot is in that half, both or elsewhere otherwise. Retain both/elsewhere in all-question denominators. Only compare first vs second where both have support. Report stricter counts additionally requiring every evidence turn to be in the pivot.
diagnostic: For the first-only and second-only question groups compute sum(activity F1 - temporal F1) in each, then max(0,sum1)+max(0,sum2)-max(0,sum1+sum2). Scale by all original comparisons. This is the descriptive extra F1 from a question-aware choice between the two existing whole-session trajectories over the best common choice on those questions. No counterfactual mixed writer return is identified. Record opposite preferences, coverage and question counts by history, and preserve exact identifiers/answers for follow-up. An experiment with half-specific writes needs freshly executed matched trajectories and question-blind actions.
